claim_scope: CPU score-surface kill test of DVI's cheap-localization assumption and persistent repair-page reuse
research_question: At operational candidate depths, how often does the cheap text locator miss evidence that visual retrieval finds, and do those visually repairable evidence pages recur in future queries?

relevance_semantics.query_hit: at least one positive-qrel page occurs within the candidate depth
relevance_semantics.weighted_recall: qrel mass inside the candidate depth divided by total qrel mass
relevance_semantics.repairable_escape: text has no relevant page at K while complete visual retrieval has at least one
relevance_semantics.repair_page: a relevant page inside visual Top-K and outside text Top-K for a repairable-escape query

cross_fit.history_role: define previously observed repair pages only
cross_fit.future_role: measure future repair-page event and unique-page overlap

optimistic_dvi_proxy.semantics: scan text-ranked candidates until the first relevant page or K; assumes perfect answer verification and is therefore a lower bound on pages analyzed
optimistic_dvi_proxy.warning: No VLM-QA accuracy or latency is fabricated from retrieval score surfaces.

gate.meaning: Only if two domains show material cheap-locator escape, visual repair, and reusable repair evidence should a defer-materialize cost crossover be built.

information_boundary.complete_visual_scores: oracle diagnostic only; forbidden to a realizable materialization policy
